why: Quantfury publishes no tax line and §56 leaves every tax to the client. The tax map charged 0.40 % French FTT on 66 lines and 0.50 % British stamp on one, and on those lines the tax was about 94 % of the modelled round trip — fifteen times the book. Nobody had ever seen it debited. This trip is the test. It had to straddle a session close: the French FTT falls on the net daily acquisition, so an intraday buy and sell cancel out and would owe nothing whatever Quantfury does.

expect.note: Sell 15 at the bid on the next session and reconcile: balance change minus (sell - 18.465) * 15 converted. A shortfall near 1.11 EUR is the FTT; a shortfall near zero means Quantfury debits no transfer tax and the 66 French lines are overstated fifteenfold.

reconcile.verdict: The closed-position sheet and the cash movement are the overnight price, 18.465 → 18.41. Nothing near 1.11 EUR was taken. Quantfury does not debit the French FTT.

alsoWatch.what: the side the fill lands on, which is what the whole cost model rests on
alsoWatch.seen: The ticket quoted 18.465 / 18.470 and the position opened at 18.465 — the bid, on a buy — and marks at 0.00 unrealised against a bid still at 18.465. PETR4 did the same thing on 15 September: quoted 49.12 / 49.14, filled 49.12. If a buy really lands on the bid rather than the ask, a round trip does not cross the book and `usd` overstates every one of the 2 030 lines by a full spread. Two fills are not enough to tell that from a half-tick of drift, so the close is the third point. Watch whether the sell lands on the bid too, and what the reconciliation leaves unexplained.
alsoWatch.close: The sell ticket showed 18.405 / 18.420 and the fill is 18.41 — the bid, half a tick inside. Three fills, all on the bid: two buys (PETR4, ACA) and this sell. An overnight move of 5.5 cents swamps the 0.5-cent book, so this trip cannot zero the spread; it can only say the crossing assumption is the one that keeps being contradicted.
